Executives see no AI impact
stories.summary: Eighty percent of executives report seeing no impact from AI on their productivity. The disconnect may be due to where they are looking for results. The search continues.

stories.title: Prototypes are the new requirements
stories.summary: Building a working version of a feature now takes an afternoon, meaning the prototype often precedes the formal requirements document. Teams are finishing the work before the review meeting even starts. The document is now a souvenir of the process.

stories.title: The rise of AI design slop
stories.summary: Designers are navigating a 2026 landscape where AI has transformed UX in unpredictable ways. The shift was the subject of a recent conference at City St George’s, University of London. The machine is being raged against.

stories.title: AX Design: The New Design Job That Barely Touches Figma - Medium
UX remains a competitive factor
stories.summary: Digital businesses are finding that a visually impressive website is insufficient for winning customers. Confusing interfaces and slow checkouts continue to drive users away. As AI accelerates product development, user experience is becoming a primary factor in business competition.

stories.title: The user is no longer the judge
stories.summary: AI has collapsed the time required to build models. The individuals who previously defined what was correct have disappeared along with the development timeline. The middle has been removed.

stories.title: How do architects and interior designers divide responsibilities on a building project? - Britannica
Allo typeface released for interfaces
stories.summary: Allo is a free, open-source typeface designed for screens and interfaces. It allows designers to adjust weight, roundness, and optical sizing while maintaining readability. The project is available on GitHub for use in text, displays, and code.

stories.title: A new national font, Zakon, was unveiled in Ukraine - Visit Ukraine.Today
Ukraine develops national typeface
stories.summary: Ukraine has introduced a national typeface to replace the use of Russian fonts. The project aims to establish a distinct visual identity for the country. The font is now available for use.

stories.title: Typespotting returns to Milan
stories.summary: The Typespotting gathering has returned to Milan to focus on independent typography. Designers and studios are presenting their work and sharing technical workflows, including the transition from analog sketches to vector files. The event aims to connect local creatives with the international lettering circuit.

stories.title: Werklig designs Voltcore identity
stories.summary: Helsinki studio Werklig has created the brand identity for Finnish energy company Voltcore. The visual system uses a three-column grid and monospaced typography to represent engineering. The design relies on white space and typographic contrast rather than cards or shadows.

stories.title: Interval Type releases Sugarspark and Sugarswift
stories.summary: Interval Type has launched a 22-cut typeface family consisting of the retro-futurist display font Sugarspark and the functional text font Sugarswift. The designs draw from sixties and seventies modernism. The system covers both Latin and Cyrillic scripts.

stories.title: SomeOne reimagines Co-op identity
stories.summary: Design studio SomeOne has updated the Co-op brand identity by breaking the existing cloverleaf symbol into five distinct Membershapes. The redesign aims to highlight the cooperative's member-ownership model, which has been in place since 1844. The pieces are designed to function independently.

stories.title: Johnson Banks redesigns RIBA identity
stories.summary: Johnson Banks has created a new brand identity for RIBA using negative space to form typographic characters. The letters are constructed from the gaps between shapes, intended to mirror architectural principles. The mark is designed to remain legible from tote bags to building banners.

stories.title: Pentagram updates Poetry Foundation identity
stories.summary: Pentagram has redesigned the Poetry Foundation brand identity by stripping back the organization's century-old Pegasus emblem. The new system features a redrawn mark and central-axis type stacks. The Pegasus is now used as a primary brand element rather than a corner crest.

stories.title: Canva lets users opt out of AI features
stories.summary: Canva has introduced settings allowing users to disable generative AI features and reduce AI-generated content in their design libraries. The controls are available to all users at no extra cost, as the platform seeks to provide more flexibility regarding the role of AI in creative processes.

stories.title: Canva added an AI ‘kill switch’ to its tools - Fast Company
Adobe discusses the evolving role of the creative professional
stories.summary: Adobe continues to integrate AI tools like Firefly into its creative suite. Vice President Deepa Subramaniam says the company aims to empower creative choice while serving an industry where the definition of a professional has shifted from classically trained veterans to a broader, democratised user base.

stories.title: Adobe doesn’t want to force AI down your throat
stories.summary: When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission. Over the years, the definition of the 'creative' has been in flux. No longer comprised of classically trained industry veterans, design has been democratised (for better or for worse, depending on who you

stories.title: Adobe previews local AI integration for creative tools
stories.summary: Adobe has previewed Local MCP Integration, allowing external AI agents to directly control Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, and After Effects. The company says this enables AI to perform tasks like rotoscoping and filling image blanks by calling out to Adobe functions from outside the software environment.

stories.title: AI coding agents struggle in simulated workplace tests
stories.summary: AI coding agents are nearing top scores on standard benchmarks but complete fewer than one in ten tasks in a simulated workplace environment. While Anthropic claims Claude writes over 80 percent of its production code, simulated colleagues and project boards appear to present a different set of challenges.

stories.title: METR warns of risks in AI research acceleration
stories.summary: Research organization METR warns that AI models are improving at research tasks faster than experts can safely measure. The group states that current data is insufficient to rule out a drastic acceleration, potentially leaving humans unable to understand or react to catastrophic risks posed by new systems.

stories.title: Ageism in data and design limits AI adoption for older adults
stories.summary: Research from NSTU suggests that biased datasets and interface designs tailored to younger users hinder generative AI adoption among people over 50. While usage in this demographic grew to 30 percent in 2025, many find the responses poorly suited to their needs and contexts.

stories.title: OpenAI updates prompting tips for Astra and Sol models
stories.summary: OpenAI has released new prompt templates for its Astra and Sol models to address issues with overly brief answers and unnecessary questioning. The company advises developers to instruct models to reuse existing code and avoid abstractions, noting that editing conversation history can impact token costs and quality.

stories.title: Figma revenue grows 48 percent year over year
stories.summary: Figma reported second-quarter revenue of $370.1 million, a 48 percent increase compared to the previous year. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to $1.467 billion, noting that over half of its high-value paid customers now use its AI agent on a weekly basis.

stories.title: Figma CFO sells shares
stories.summary: Figma CFO and Treasurer Praveer Melwani recently sold approximately $2.1 million in company stock. The transaction represented 7.4 percent of the executive's holdings and was executed at a price above the current market value of $15.77 per share.

stories.title: Figma and Fastly compete for cloud market share
stories.summary: Figma and Fastly are both positioning themselves as essential tools for digital transformation through 2027. While Figma maintains higher revenue growth through its collaborative design ecosystem, Fastly continues to see significant adoption across media and entertainment sectors within the edge cloud market.

stories.title: Canva resolves subscription management issue
stories.summary: Canva confirmed that an incident affecting users attempting to manage their subscriptions has been resolved. The company provided updates throughout the process after users reported difficulties with billing and subscription components on the platform.

stories.title: How to Fix Canva Not Loading on Your Device
stories.summary: To fix Canva not loading, check for a Canva outage, reopen its browser tabs, then check your connection and update your browser or app. If Canva still will not open, try a private browser window before clearing cached data or changing browser settings. stories.summary: To create a QR code in Canva, open a design, select Apps, search for QR code, choose Static QR codes, enter your destination in URL, and select Save. Choose Dynamic QR codes instead when you need to change the destination later. Both types are available across Canva plans, though advanced

stories.title: AI agents move into text messaging
stories.summary: A growing number of AI agents are being designed to function directly within text messaging apps. These tools aim to handle scheduling, research, and shopping without requiring users to download dedicated software. Instinct currently leads the space with a $10 billion valuation following recent funding.

stories.title: Designers shift to pen.dev for browser-based workflows
stories.summary: The design blog Abduzeedo reports that it has replaced Figma with pen.dev for its daily workflow. The platform uses a WebGL canvas and live shaders to simulate real product design, which the authors claim provides a faster and more familiar environment for those with coding experience.

stories.title: BMW iX4 design patented in India
stories.summary: The BMW iX4 design has been patented in India, hinting at a potential launch after its international release in March 2027. The coupe-SUV will offer three configurations and battery options up to 108.7kWh. It is expected to be priced between Rs 90 lakh and 95 lakh.

stories.title: India building automation market projected to hit $12.56 billion by 2030
stories.summary: India’s building automation market is expected to grow from $4.32 billion in 2025 to $12.56 billion by 2030. Industry reports suggest IoT-enabled automation in commercial offices will rise to 45% by 2030, with digital optimisation offering potential energy savings of up to 40 percent.

stories.title: AAFT Online launches interior design diploma
stories.summary: AAFT Online has introduced a one-year diploma program in interior design. The course combines live classes, practical projects, and industry mentorship. The curriculum aims to move beyond basic room decoration to address the technical planning and coordination required for modern design careers.

stories.title: NID DAT 2027 exam topics outlined
stories.summary: The National Institute of Design has detailed the focus areas for its 2027 Design Aptitude Test. The exam evaluates drawing skills, creativity, and problem-solving through topics including object drawing, product development, and visual storytelling. Candidates are encouraged to organize their preparation around these specific design-based competencies.

stories.title: Consumer commission orders refund for Livspace customer
stories.summary: A consumer commission ordered a refund for a homeowner who paid Rs 71.62 lakh for a renovation, citing inferior materials and a falling kitchen shutter. The ruling follows reports of disputed vendor payments, financial losses, and layoffs at the firm. The company has not commented on the history.

stories.title: Ambedkar Bhavan project nears completion after 14 years
stories.summary: Construction on Mysuru’s Ambedkar Bhavan is expected to finish in two months, 14 years after the project began. Work stalled in 2020 due to a funding shortage before the Mysuru Development Authority resumed the project last year. Officials report that 80 percent of the work is finished.

stories.title: QR codes for wedding invitations explained
stories.summary: Couples are increasingly using QR codes to share wedding details like venue, date, and RSVP links. The scannable squares allow hosts to provide extensive information without cluttering physical invitation cards. Guests access the data by scanning the code with their smartphone cameras.

stories.title: Domicil opens new store in Kolkata
stories.summary: German luxury furniture brand Domicil has opened a retail location at Spacio Tower in Kolkata. The expansion marks the brand's latest effort to strengthen its presence in eastern India. The store showcases collections emphasizing German craftsmanship, material selection, and functional design sensibilities.

stories.title: The Senator Group India debuts Kaya office seating
stories.summary: The Senator Group India has launched its Kaya office seating collection, developed with design studio Pearson Lloyd. The range focuses on lightweight construction and ergonomic comfort as an alternative to chairs requiring multiple technical adjustments. It aims to address the rise of shared desks in modern Indian workplaces.

stories.title: Exclusive | Genesis AI, a Robotics Startup, Raises $500 Million - WSJ
Genesis AI secures $500 million in Series A funding
stories.summary: Genesis AI has raised $500 million in Series A funding at a $3.5 billion valuation. The company is developing Eno, a robot with a modular design that avoids a human-like head. Genesis is prioritizing U.S. supply chains and contract manufacturing before considering expansion into European markets.

stories.title: Redbrick Offices raises Rs 630 crore
stories.summary: Managed workspace provider Redbrick Offices has secured Rs 630 crore in equity across its Series A and A1 rounds. The funding was led by India SME Investments and Abakkus Asset Manager. The company previously operated as a bootstrapped business for several years.

stories.title: Former Bewakoof CEO launches AI shopping tool
stories.summary: Prabhkiran Singh has launched Save8, an AI-powered assistant designed to compare prices across ecommerce platforms. The venture follows Singh’s departure from Bewakoof after 14 years. He is currently in talks with investors to raise external capital for the new shopping platform.

stories.title: Sarvam AI launches Token Factory platform
stories.summary: Sarvam AI has launched Token Factory, a commercial platform providing developers access to multiple AI models. The service aims to capture demand for AI inference by serving models on local infrastructure. The company is now shifting its focus toward usage-driven revenues.

stories.title: Startup sues Apple over NameDrop patent
stories.summary: GG Technologies has filed a lawsuit against Apple in the Bombay High Court, alleging that the NameDrop feature infringes on its patent. The startup claims it developed the contact-sharing technology years before Apple introduced it. The firm is seeking to have the feature disabled in India.

stories.title: Sarvam AI faces scrutiny over model hosting
stories.summary: Sarvam AI is facing criticism regarding the economics and model selection of its new Token Factory platform. Critics have questioned the inclusion of Chinese models and the source of hardware used for the service. The company maintains that it is using its own infrastructure for the platform.

stories.title: VC funding for Indian startups hits $255 million
stories.summary: Venture capital investment in Indian startups rose to $255 million in the third week of November, up from $26 million the previous week. AI, retail, and spacetech sectors led the activity. Quantum computing is also emerging as a focus for potential energy sector applications.

stories.title: NIUDIAN wins international design award
stories.summary: Shandong Niudian Automotive Technology received the Supreme Design Award at the 2026 International Product Green Award. The company was recognized for its NIUDIAN Pickup K1 electric cabin vehicle. The award highlights the firm's position within China's electric vehicle manufacturing sector.

stories.title: Canva reportedly cut jobs before 1,271 redundancies
stories.summary: Canva reportedly carried out unannounced job cuts and saw increased employee exits in the two months before its November 4 restructuring announcement. The company stated that 1,271 positions were affected, though insiders suggest the total reduction in workforce is significantly higher. The math is proving difficult to reconcile.

stories.title: Canva layoffs may exceed 1,271 announced cuts
stories.summary: Canva announced a 22 percent workforce reduction on November 4, but reports suggest the total number of departures is higher. Employees claim the company quietly dismissed staff and left vacancies unfilled in the preceding months. The official count appears to be a work in progress.

stories.title: Canva dismissed staff before formal restructuring
stories.summary: Canva reportedly dismissed employees in the months leading up to its November 4 announcement of 1,271 job cuts. Sources claim the company was reducing its workforce through quiet terminations and performance management processes before the formal restructuring began. The company has not clarified the total number of exits.

stories.title: Canva reportedly cut jobs quietly before redundancies
stories.summary: Canva reportedly saw a rise in unannounced terminations and employee exits in the two months before its November 4 restructuring. While the company announced 1,271 redundancies, insiders claim the actual workforce reduction is higher. The company has not provided a revised figure for the total departures.

stories.title: Canva staff report secret sackings before layoffs
stories.summary: Canva employees claim the company conducted secret sackings in the months before announcing widespread redundancies. Insiders allege that these departures mean the total number of staff cuts this year is far greater than the figures made public by the company. The positivity cult has hit a wall.

What does a user interface designer do
stories.summary: User interface designers create the visual elements and layouts for websites, apps, and wearable devices. The role focuses on shaping the aesthetics and functionality of digital products to ensure they are navigable and intuitive for users. The skillset remains in demand for creating seamless digital experiences.
